Financial institutions typically monitor employee behavior to check for unusual activity. For example, it would be unusual for most employees to wire large sums of money into or out of their country of domicile on a regular basis. Because of the volume and the speed of the transactions, funds transfer activity is considered particularly vulnerable to money laundering and fraudulent activity resulting from inappropriate employee behavior. This scenario detects funds transferred between accounts either owned by employees or employee family members and:
- All unrelated parties - Any employee or employee-related account that is not within the employee's country of domicile
This scenario considers both debits and credits for Electronic Funds Transfers (EFTs). Debits and credits are treated in absolute values, disregarding whether the value is positive or negative.
